features: The file icon theme chosen in Settings → Appearance now also applies to Source Control's file and folder rows, including changes, staged files and commit history.
A task's Word documents now open read-only in a tab of its worktree, laid out like Word, with Open in Default App as a fallback.
Any .docx opened from the explorer uses the same Word viewer, including on a paired Orca server; old .doc files and files over 3 MB still open in the browser.
The «Take to work» dialog's Agent line lets you pick which Claude account of the worktree's host starts the session, without changing the host's selected account.
fixes: A task's Word documents no longer open in the browser at the console's address instead of inside Orca.
Tab bar → «Claude — account» on a paired server's workspace now starts Claude with that account instead of System default; older servers hide these items until updated.

features: Settings → Appearance → File Icons lets the Explorer show Material Icon Theme icons for files and folders, with light variants on light backgrounds.
The new-tab menu offers «Claude — account» entries to start Claude under another account on the workspace's host for that session only.
The Mockups tab on a build-web task card is now called Artifacts.
The status chip on a build-web task card, full screen or in the side panel, now opens a picker with every available status.
New build-web notifications such as failed builds, console errors or task comments appear as a desktop banner, or as a toast while Orca is in front.
settings: Settings → Appearance gets a File Icons option to choose between Orca's own icons and the Material Icon Theme in the Explorer.
Settings → Notifications gets «build-web» for desktop banners and «build-web Inside Orca» for in-app toasts, both for build-web notifications.
fixes: The plan spec's link to open a task now works again, opening the task's card by its title instead of a removed full-screen button.

features: The titlebar now shows a build-web notifications bell beside the sidebar toggle, with a red unread count for failed builds, console errors and updates to your tasks.
Opening the titlebar bell marks notifications as read; clicking one opens its task's card, and Clear empties the list for you only.
A new tasks icon in the titlebar counts running stand jobs, image builds and test runs, and lists recently finished ones with their status.
Clicking an entry in the titlebar tasks list opens a console job's live log with Cancel, a build's task card, or a test run's console page.
settings: Settings → Integrations can show or hide the titlebar notifications and tasks icons; by default they follow the Issues setting, and they can be hidden from the context menu.
fixes: A task card opened from the titlebar no longer closes on its own the first time a build-web page loads.
In a narrow sidebar header the app name now shortens with an ellipsis instead of cutting off the controls beside it.

features: Right-clicking the status bar now offers "Usage from", letting you pin the usage meters to this computer or a paired server instead of following the focused workspace.
Right-clicking the status bar now offers "All Claude & Codex Accounts", showing a separate usage chip for every account on the chosen host, active account first.
The Claude and Codex account switchers now follow the same host as the usage meters and show usage for that host's inactive accounts.
An unreachable server's accounts in the status bar keep their last usage numbers, marked as stale.
The status bar's usage limit chips now turn green, yellow or red depending on how much of each limit has been used.
Stats & Usage has a picker to show usage for this computer, a paired server, or this computer and all servers together.
fixes: Stats & Usage now counts Claude sessions stored in a custom Claude config folder, which were previously missing from the totals.

features: The status bar shows each connected Orca server's CPU and memory use, with a red dot when either reaches 90% and grey when unreachable.
Issues page: clicking a task title opens its full card as a tab beside a List tab, and open tabs are restored after restarting.
Issues page: clicking the star column header sorts favorite tasks first, and a second click reverses the order.
Live Claude usage now works even when you have your own Claude status line or start Claude with your own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR folder.
The command line can add a Claude account from an existing signed-in folder and give it a name.
settings: Settings → Accounts → Add Folder saves a Claude account from an already signed-in folder on the host, including on remote servers.
Settings → Accounts lets you rename Claude accounts, and the name replaces the email in Settings, the status-bar switcher and switch notices.

features: Each number on the sidebar's Issues, Images, Trains and Testing items now has its own tooltip explaining what it counts.
A page history button pair with a recent-pages list (⟲ ← →) now sits beside the workspace Back/Forward, letting you return to Orca's pages, task cards and recap reports.
Task numbers in Recaps reports are now links that open the task's card full screen, and task-type cells show as coloured chips.
A task's full-screen card, including over the Testing list, now has Plan and Mockups tabs showing the task's plan and its mockup pages.
fixes: The Sidebar → Issues number now counts only open blockers among the tasks the page shows, no longer including done or won't-fix tasks.
In development builds, a task card opened from a link in Issues or Testing no longer closes immediately on its own.

features: Images: clicking «failed» on an image row offers to settle it with the newest successful build of the same image, without rebuilding anything.
fixes: Issues and Testing: Back now reopens the task card you opened an attachment or agent session from, on the same tab and layout.

features: Source Control → branch menu offers «Update from <base>», which fetches the base branch and merges it in, fast-forwarding when the branch has no commits of its own.
Issues → a task's card lists its attached files and each comment's files, opening Markdown, HTML, pictures, PDFs and text in tabs of the task's worktree.
Editor → the line-number menu offers «Git Blame», showing who last changed each line beside the editor, with commit details on hover and the change on click.
Source Control → in the tree view, folders can collapse or expand all their subfolders, section headers fold all folders, and Alt+click toggles a whole subtree.
Images → any successful build can be picked, and «Copy links» copies each image's registry reference with its build number, warning about ones not pushed yet.

fixes: Issues → «Take to work» into a new worktree on a server now opens that worktree and starts its session instead of saying it could not open it.
The Services tab in the right sidebar now stays selected after resizing the panel instead of switching back to Explorer.

features: A new Services tab in the right panel runs a repository's dev services, letting you start profiles, restart, stop, view consoles, open services, and release slots.
Dev services commands configured in a repository's orca.yaml must be trusted like setup scripts, and are re-checked on every run, including on remote hosts.
Testing now opens on two tabs: «In testing» shows the current watch, and «Test history» lists past runs by day, filterable by All, Nightly or Manual.
Testing → Test history opens a run with its changes since the previous run, a workspace map, a per-test breakdown, each test's last 14 runs, job logs and junit.xml.
The sidebar's Testing item shows, in red, how many tests failed in the newest finished nightly run.
The sidebar's Trains item shows how many images are in windows that are building or deploying right now.
A task opened from Testing now gets a wider dialog, up to 1536 pixels across.
Recaps now opens as a month calendar showing each report on the day it finished; click one to open it, then Escape returns to the calendar.
Recaps has a «Calendar | List» switch, remembers the view you picked, and applies the product, version and automation filters to the calendar too.
A new sidebar item, «Stands», lists the AP, DC and SA stands, with each stand's services, their state, image, tag, build number and build date.
Stands lets you restart one service or bring the whole stand up again, after confirming, and follows the job and its log on the page.
Stands shows a service's log with a choice of how many recent lines to load, live following, and Cmd/Ctrl+F search with highlights.
Stands → Users lists a stand's UI logins, filterable by application; «Log in» opens the stand in Orca's browser and fills in the login form.
Application chips on Stands use the same colours as on Issues: SA purple, DC blue and AP green.
The build log dialog on Images uses the new log viewer, so you can search it with Cmd/Ctrl+F.
In a train window, each image now shows whether it is «pushed», «built, not pushed» or «held», with the reason it was held.
The source editor supports go to definition across files for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python, with Cmd/Ctrl+click, F12 and Peek.
The source editor has Back and Forward buttons and shortcuts for moving between the places you jumped to, including mouse side buttons.
The source editor has an Outline panel beside the code, toggled from the editor header, with a filter, the current symbol highlighted, and click-to-jump.
«Take to work» names the session after its tasks' keys and titles, and taking the same tasks again reopens that session.
settings: The «Work in this worktree» option in the «Take to work» dialog is removed, along with its remembered choice.
fixes: The images in a train window now update as each build finishes, instead of keeping their old state while another image is still building.
Pushing an image now updates the train window, and its tags column no longer lists tags of images that were not pushed.
Images → «Push to registry» now sends every picked build even if one is refused; refused images are named and stay selected.
«Take to work» no longer lets the task skill create its own worktree; Orca creates one only when you choose «Create a new worktree».
When «Take to work» creates a new worktree, its base branch is always chosen from the repository's branches, and the session starts only once one is picked.

releases.note: Everything this custom build adds to Orca
features: The main menu has a new «Changelog» item right after «About Orca», listing each release's new features, settings and fixes, with the installed one marked.
A new «Issues» sidebar page lists build-web tasks with Mine, For AI, Favorites, Jira and To work quick filters, status and product filters, search and stars.
Issues → task list shows coloured chips, sortable columns, pages of 50, an assignee column, and status, priority and assignee changeable straight from the row.
Issues → task list marks tasks handed to AI or held by an agent session, and shows subtasks folded under their task with a subtask count.
The Issues sidebar item counts open top-priority blockers among the tasks matching the page's current filters.
Clicking a task in Issues opens a resizable side card where the title, description, steps, status, priority, assignee, release and «handed to AI» are edited in place.
A task opens full screen with Overview, Build, Guide & Jira, Commits and Subtasks tabs, laid out like build-web's own task card.
Task card → Overview has comments with a composer that can also post to Jira, and your own comments can be corrected or deleted.
Task card → Build adopts or creates a run, shows image freshness and progress, and builds, rebuilds, cancels, removes and publishes images, with build logs in a dialog.
Task card → Guide generates and revises the guide live, takes screenshots from a chosen stand, and publishes it to the task's Jira issue.
Task card → Properties sets assignee, product, stand, release, type, priority and build destination, and subtasks inherit the rest from their parent.
Task card → Subtasks lists each subtask with an in-place status, and warns while open subtasks block moving the task onward.
Card panels and commit lists in the full-screen task card resize by dragging or arrow keys, and their widths are remembered per tab.
«Take to work» sends picked tasks to a new Claude session in an existing or new worktree, named after the task keys.
«Take to work» on a task whose session is still open switches to that session instead of starting a second one.
A new «Images» sidebar page shows each image's newest build with filters, sortable columns, build history and push to the registry.
The Images sidebar item counts images building now and, in a red chip, images whose newest build failed.
Images → build dialog starts a new image build, prefilled from the last build, with a «Run tests» option that is off by default.
Images shows each push's progress in a card with per-image results and its log, then refreshes the table when the push finishes.
Images has «in progress» and «failed» filters by last build status, and build logs open in a dialog that follows the newest lines.
A new «Trains» sidebar page lists build-web's build trains with their windows, a «What boards now» preview and a «Depart now» button.
Trains → a history row opens its window in a «Run» dialog with status, images, tasks, errors, publications and the journal on request.
A new «Testing» sidebar page lists tasks in testing whose images are not yet out, with «Check now» and chips showing the work left.
Testing → the work-left chips open the push or build menu directly, and a task opens in a dialog over the list.
A new «Recaps» sidebar page lists finished build-web automation reports, newest first, filterable by product, version, automation and date range.
Recaps → the selected report shows beside the list in a resizable panel, with its charts and diagrams, following Orca's theme.
A new «Git» page shows every branch's commit log with a graph, branch tree, changed files and diffs, plus branch and commit operations.
Custom builds now update from build-web's «Orca» feed instead of GitHub, and an offered update links to build-web's release page.
An app window that is older than its loaded code now asks you to restart instead of showing a cryptic error.
settings: Settings → Notifications has a new «Only When an Agent Needs Input» switch, off by default, limiting alerts and the Dock badge to agents waiting on you.
Settings → Integrations has a Build Web card to connect, test, replace or disconnect build-web and to bring back hidden Issues, Images, Trains, Testing or Recaps items.
fixes: A remote server no longer fails to start its Orca daemon after its third daemon update.
Custom builds can again deploy to servers over SSH and are no longer treated as older than the newest official release.
The Trains sidebar item now appears for people already connected to build-web, following the Issues item until set on its own.
The Issues sidebar item now opens the task list instead of the card left open, and the card's breadcrumb returns to the list.
The Images sidebar count now refreshes within a minute, and immediately on build-web pages or after starting a build.
Long lines in a commit diff now wrap inside their own column instead of running over the other side.
Resizable column splits in task card tabs no longer stop dragging immediately after you start.
